  "text": "The constable counted the knocks on his fingers. When he reached five, he tucked his hand under his arm.

“Don’t answer,” Ada said.

“I wasn’t going to.”

Something scraped beneath the boards, moving from the yellow door toward the place where Venn stood. He stepped aside. A nail rose slowly through the wood, bright and clean, then sank again.

Elias crouched without touching the floor. “It’s looking for a way out.”

Ada tried to lift the ring from the groove. It held fast. Around it, the stone had begun to pale, as though frost were spreading through its grain.

“Was that Mara’s ring?” the constable asked.

“No.” Ada pulled once more. “Mine.”

Beneath them came a soft, delighted laugh. The constable backed into the wall.

Venn took the iron poker from the cold hearth. “Tell me where to strike.”

Ada looked at the row of boards. The scraping had stopped directly under her feet. She could feel a small weight pressing upward against her soles, testing them.

“Nowhere,” she said. “We leave the ring and get out.”

The constable reached the stairs first. Elias followed, dragging Venn by the sleeve. Ada was last. At the foot of the stairs, she glanced back.

A narrow strip of light showed beneath the yellow door. On the boards before it lay five sooty marks, no larger than a child’s fingertips.

Then the marks lifted from the wood. One by one, they appeared on the bottom stair."
